The Statistic
Net Wins — a player's share of their team's margin, scaled to wins
Traditional stats measure what a player does. Net Wins measures what that production was worth — expressed as a share of the team's net statistical margin, multiplied by how many games that margin actually won.
Player Net Actions
(PTS+REB+AST+BLK+STL) − (Missed FG+Missed FT+TOV+PF)
Team Net Actions
Team positive actions − Team negative actions (same formula, full roster)
Net Wins = (Player Net Actions ÷ Team Net Actions) × Team Wins
Example: Cade Cunningham, 2025-26 — 1,521 net actions ÷ 9,720 team net actions = 15.6% share × 60 wins = 9.39 net wins
What this metric measures
Net Wins measures a player's share of their team's net statistical margin — the difference between everything the team did right and everything it did wrong — scaled to how many wins that margin actually produced. It is a contextual share metric, not a causal wins-added stat.
What it doesn't claim
Net Wins does not isolate individual causation from team quality — a player on a 60-win team earns a share of 60 wins. A player with identical stats on a 20-win team earns fewer net wins because their team's margin produced fewer wins. Team context is preserved by design, not removed. Use avg/season and peak metrics to compare across different team environments.
Implied statistics
The formula captures more than the box score records. Screens, defensive rotations, box-outs, and communication that never appear in counting stats show up implicitly — because they contribute to the team's net margin, and that margin is the denominator. This is why players like Dennis Rodman (#76 combined) and Horace Grant (#47) rank significantly higher than their raw counting stats would suggest. The reverse is also true: Luka Dončić ranks #138 despite elite counting stats, because the defensive breakdowns and losing contexts his teams experienced compress the team net margin he's measured against.
Data & edge case notes
Pre-1974 player BLK/STL are not tracked and default to 0 (editable). For seasons where a team's net actions total falls below 1,000 — a small number of historically anomalous seasons (38 of 1,818 team-seasons) — the season's league-median net actions figure is substituted to prevent division instability. This affects fewer than 2% of team-seasons and is flagged in the underlying data.

Pre-1977 Turnover Correction
The NBA did not track turnovers before 1977-78, so pre-1977 seasons are missing roughly 23% of their negative actions. This slider scales the team loss-rate denominator to compensate, making each recorded negative action cost proportionally more losses. Default 1.29× reflects the league-average TOV share derived from post-1977 data. Slide left to 1.00× to remove the correction; slide right for a more aggressive adjustment.
Correction factor: 1.29×
